title: Infra: make domains and the staging branch optional in the site template; document the console repo-connect step
description:
FINDINGS from the Amplify connect test (2026-10-06, Ryan + orchestrator):
1. PROVEN: an Amplify app created with NO repository can have a repo connected afterwards via the console's Amplify GitHub App flow (same app id; repository, service role and a first build were set; build SUCCEEDED). So the design stands: the infra template creates apps repo-less and token-free; a human does one GitHub connection per app.
2. CAVEAT: the console changed the app's platform from WEB_COMPUTE to WEB when connecting a README-only repo (framework auto-detection). A real Next.js repo should detect as WEB_COMPUTE but verify after connecting; fix with 'aws amplify update-app --app-id <id> --platform WEB_COMPUTE'. Put both in docs/site-hosting.md's runbook.
3. The console wizard asks for a service role and build settings; for template apps these are already set by the template (service role, generated build spec), so the human should only do the GitHub connection. In the test the console created a NEW service role (amplifyconsole-backend-role, AdministratorAccess-Amplify): when connecting a template app, verify the app keeps the template's service role (check iamServiceRoleArn before/after) so the console does not replace it.
4. TEMPLATE LIMITATION (found by the deploy agent): AmplifyAppShellStack always creates two AWS::Amplify::Domain resources (newsroom.<domain> on main, staging.<domain> on staging) and a staging branch; cms.domainName, hostedZoneId, repository and OAuth redirect URLs are required by parseSiteConfig. A first/scratch deploy therefore needs real domains (certificate + DNS verification wait). Make domains and the staging branch optional (e.g. cms.domainName optional; skip Domain resources when absent) so a site can be stood up and proven without DNS, then add domains later. Add tests (synth with and without domains) and update the docs.
right_now_summary: The template is being updated for repo-free, domain-free setups, with console connection steps documented.
